subject: A Level Biology
title: Action potential
question:
Fig. 9.1 shows the changes in potential across the membrane of a neurone during an action potential.
(a) Name the stages labelled A, B, C and D.
(b) Explain the movement of ions that causes stage A.
(c) Explain why stage C occurs.

scene: The curve uses the graph option that never overshoots, so it stays flat at rest.
First try: label C sat on top of the curve.
Second try: moved C below and to the right.
tikz: First try: label D sat on the dashed threshold line.
Second try: moved D below the resting line.

figure:
A graph on a grid. Horizontal axis: time / ms, from 0 to 5. Vertical axis: membrane potential / mV, from −90 to +50, marked every 20 from −80 to 40.
The membrane potential starts flat at −70 mV, rises sharply after about 0.8 ms to a peak of about +35 mV at 1.6 ms, and falls quickly to dip below rest to about −80 mV at about 2.6 ms. It then recovers back to −70 mV by about 3.6 ms and stays flat.
A dashed horizontal line at −55 mV, labelled threshold.
Use label lines with letters only: A to the rising phase, B to the falling phase, C to the dip below rest and D to the flat resting part after recovery.
Caption: Fig. 9.1.
